newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jordan's Hussein backs role for Europe in Mideast.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's Hussein backs role for Europe in Mideast.

text.p: King Hussein of Jordan has called for Europe to cooperate with the United States in the quest for a Middle East peace, saying the region needed help from all its friends as it was "on the brink of the abyss".

In an interview with France 3 television broadcast on Friday as French President Jacques Chirac wound up his Middle East tour, the king reiterated support for Chirac's attempt to boost the role of France and Europe in Arab-Israeli negotiations.
"I think that for the sake of balance, the position of the United States can only be strengthened by the help of France and Europe," he said.

"Europe does not really want to compete with the United States. What we must aspire to is collaboration, cooperation between the two to advance the peace process...I don't think anyone will see any disadvantage," the monarch added.
In talks with Chirac, the king backed his drive to increase French and European influence provided it was in harmony with U.S. mediation efforts.

Chirac's message, well received in the Arab world, was strongly opposed in Israel. Chirac visited Syria, Israel, Palestinian autonomous territories, Jordan and Lebanon and was due to stop over in Cairo later on Friday on his way home.
Hussein said hardline Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu "told me he was committed to giving me a pleasant surprise".
"I hope he was speaking of a contribution for peace in the future, of a good surprise for a change," he added.
He said time was playing against peace, and failure to rapidly revive the peace process would lead to "real disaster".
"I fear that we will reach the psychological moment when all hopes will be lost," he said.
"We are on the brink of the abyss. Everything that has been achieved so far must absolutely not be destroyed," he said. "We must by all means reach a global settlement."
